- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrecting or lagging in mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in the middle of the forecast (days 10–20), particularly when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when true values show a downward trend or mean reversion.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price drops — fails to adjust forecast downward when true values are trending lower.
- Model overfits to recent high values, especially when the last 5–10 days are elevated — fails to recognize potential mean reversion or volatility decay.
- Model often fails to capture short-term volatility clustering — underestimates sharp drops or overestimates gradual declines.
- Model tends to smooth out noise in the data, leading to underestimation of sudden price reversals or spikes.
